note: One rubric for every candidate type. The same tasks, the same criteria, the same 1-4 scale. Scores are decision support for a human reviewer, never a pass/fail verdict.

criteria.title: Connect it to the work
criteria.description: Restates the goal, asks the questions that change the approach, names the constraint, and picks a small first step that can be checked.

levels.1: Jumps to a solution without asking what done means
levels.2: Some clarification, but no clear goal or first step
levels.4: Clear goal, sharp questions, named constraint, and a measurable first step

criteria.followUp: Ask them to name the one question whose answer would most change their approach, and why.

criteria.title: Judge the output
criteria.description: Finds the real flaw in plausible-looking AI-written code, explains the impact, proposes a fix, and says how to catch it next time.

levels.1: Approves the change or misses the flaw
levels.2: Senses something is off but does not pin it down
levels.3: Finds the flaw and the fix
levels.4: Finds the flaw, explains the blast radius, fixes it, and adds a guard

criteria.followUp: Show them a second flawed output and ask what check would have caught both.

criteria.title: Work within limits
criteria.description: Uses the access it has, stays out of what is off-limits, and asks the right owner for what it needs, with a reason.

levels.1: Uses or works around the off-limits access
levels.2: Stays in scope but stalls or guesses
levels.3: Stays in scope and makes progress with allowed tools
levels.4: Stays in scope, makes progress, and asks the right owner for exactly what it needs and why

criteria.followUp: Ask what they would do if the owner did not answer for a day.

criteria.title: Own the result
criteria.description: When something it shipped breaks: rolls back safely, says what it would monitor, tells stakeholders, and names what changes next time.

levels.1: Blames inputs or tools, no plan
levels.2: A partial plan, missing rollback, monitoring or communication
levels.4: All of that, plus what it missed and what it changes next time

criteria.followUp: Ask them to draft the two-sentence update they would send stakeholders in the first fifteen minutes.
